Gold ETFs have seen outflows in 3 of the last 5 weeks, totalling -30 tonnes net.

Last week's outflows were driven by the US's largest gold-backed ETF, $GLD, which recorded -10 tonnes in withdrawals.

US outflows totalled -12 tonnes, followed by China and the UK, both at -3 tonnes.

Global gold ETFs are now on track for their first monthly outflow in 5 months, and only their 3rd in 2026.

Traditional and onchain finance continue to converge.

As tokenization has become increasingly popular in US markets, tokenized stock on Solana can now serve as collateral.

For example, owners of Ondo's tokenized Tesla stock, $TSLA, can be utilized as collateral for DeFi lending.

This means investors can now obtain liquidity without directly selling exposure to the underlying asset.

Meanwhile, institutional activity now includes JP Morgan, BNY Mellon, State Street, and others using Solana-related infrastructure in different capacities.

This shift has driven tokenized equity supply on Solana to over $600 million, up +210% YTD despite the broader market drawdown.

Jupiter, the largest onchain platform on Solana, has reported a 72% QoQ increase in volume in these tokenized assets amid the shift.

The future of finance is quickly moving toward tokenization and more efficient transactions.

Monday was a historic trading session:

The S&P 500 outperformed the S&P 500 Equal-Weight Index by +2.1 percentage points on Monday, its largest daily outperformance since at least 1990.

This matches the +2.1 percentage-point outperformance recorded in April 2020.

At the close, the S&P 500 was up +4.7%, while the Equal-Weight Index gained +2.6%.

The divergence comes as the S&P 500 Information Technology sector led the market, surging +9.0%, its strongest daily performance since April 9th, 2025.

Nvidia, $NVDA, alone accounted for 34% of the S&P 500's return on Monday.

BREAKING: Nasdaq 100 futures extend losses to -2.5% on reports that President Trump is set to impose new tariffs on China, the EU, and 14 other countries. https://t.co/1ptRw2T6iP

We hear all the time how big bounces (like yesterday) are 'just bear market bounces '. 

But looking at past major lows and all of them started with a huge up day. 

We heard that on the 9% rally off the exact Covid lows in March 2020 and the 9% rally at the lows in April 2025. 

Going back further, a 5% spike at the lows marked the Dec '18 low and a 6% rally ended the GFC.

Who knows, but history  says a big up day indeed can end a correction or bear market.

Active asset managers aggressively rotated out of stocks last week:

The NAAIM Exposure Index is down to 51 points, its lowest since April 2025.

This measures the average exposure to US equities reported by members of the National Association of Active Investment Managers.

The index has dropped -36 points, or -41%, over the last 2 weeks, marking its largest 2-week decline since November 2023.

This brings the 4-week average of this metric down to 71 points, its lowest since March 2026.

For perspective, the index bottomed at 13 points during the 2022 bear market and 11 points during the 2020 pandemic. 

Last week's sentiment flip spanned from retail to institutions.

BREAKING: The United States now has 5,159 data centers, more than the next 9 countries with the most data centers combined.

This includes operational facilities as well as projects that are planned, under construction, or land-banked.

The US also accounts for 38.5% of the 13,384 facilities listed worldwide.

The UK and Germany rank next, with 608 and 583, respectively.

At the same time, China, France, and India have 488, 402, and 360 data centers, respectively.

Among US states, Virginia leads with 728 data centers, followed by Texas and Georgia with 605 and 308, respectively.

America is at the forefront of the global AI infrastructure expansion.
